questions.question: Where can you store files in AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon EFS (file storage) and Amazon EBS (block storage) both store files. SNS is messaging, ECS runs containers, and EMR processes big data.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to store and reliably deliver messages across distributed systems?
questions.explanation: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) stores and reliably delivers messages between distributed components. SES sends email, S3 stores objects, and Storage Gateway is hybrid storage.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the payment model that AWS makes available for customers that can commit to using Amazon EC2 over a one or 3-year term to reduce their total computing costs?
questions.explanation: The 'Save when you reserve' model lets you commit to 1- or 3-year EC2 usage (Reserved Instances/Savings Plans) for a lower rate. The other phrases describe volume or pay-as-you-go pricing, not term commitments.

questions.question: A company is migrating its on-premises database to Amazon RDS. What should the company do to ensure Amazon RDS costs are kept to a minimum?

options.text: Combine On-demand Capacity Reservations with Saving Plans.

questions.explanation: Right-sizing the database instance before and after migration ensures you only pay for the capacity you need, keeping RDS costs minimal. Multi-Region active architectures increase cost, and capacity reservations are unnecessary for a simple migration.

questions.question: What is the primary storage service used by Amazon RDS database instances?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS database instances store their data on Amazon EBS volumes. Glacier, EFS, and S3 are not the primary RDS storage layer.

questions.question: A company is developing a new application using a microservices framework. The new application is having performance and latency issues. Which AWS Service should be used to troubleshoot these issues?
questions.explanation: AWS X-Ray traces requests across microservices, helping you pinpoint performance bottlenecks and latency. CodePipeline is CI/CD, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and CloudTrail logs API calls.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services is designed with native Multi-AZ fault tolerance in mind? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB are designed with built-in, multi-AZ fault tolerance by default. Redshift and EBS are tied to a single AZ, and Snowball is a physical transfer device.

questions.question: What are the Amazon RDS features that can be used to improve the availability of your database? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ deployments (B) provide automatic failover for availability, and Read Replicas (D) offload read traffic and can be promoted. Automatic patching and Edge Locations do not directly improve RDS availability in this sense.

questions.question: Sarah has deployed an application in the Northern California (us-west-1) region. After examining the application’s traffic, she notices that about 30% of the traffic is coming from Asia. What can she do to reduce latency for the users in Asia?

options.text: Replicate the current resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same region.
Migrate the application to a hosting provider in Asia.
Create a CDN using CloudFront, so that content is cached at Edge Locations close to and in Asia.

questions.explanation: Creating a CloudFront CDN caches content at Edge Locations near Asian users, reducing their latency without moving the application. Multi-AZ replication and recreating content do not address geographic latency.

questions.question: An organization runs many systems and uses many AWS products. Which of the following services enables them to control how each developer interacts with these products?
questions.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls how each developer (user/role) can interact with AWS services and resources through permissions. RDS, NACLs, and EMR do not manage developer permissions.

questions.question: Using Amazon EC2 falls under which of the following cloud computing models?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers you manage yourself, which is Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS). PaaS and SaaS abstract away more of the stack.

questions.question: Which of the below is a best-practice when building applications on AWS?

options.text: Strengthen physical security by applying the principle of least privilege.
Ensure that the application runs on hardware from trusted vendors.
Use IAM policies to maintain performance.
Decouple the components of the application so that they run independently.

questions.explanation: Decoupling application components so they run independently is an AWS best practice that improves resilience and scalability. Least privilege is for security, not physical hardware, and IAM policies are not a performance tool.

questions.question: Your company is designing a new application that will store and retrieve photos and videos. Which of the following services should you recommend as the underlying storage mechanism?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is the recommended store for photos and videos (large, unstructured objects). EBS attaches to one instance, SQS is a queue, and Instance Store is ephemeral.

questions.question: Amazon Glacier is an Amazon S3 storage class that is suitable for storing [...] & [...]. (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Glacier suits active archives (A) and long-term analytic data (C) — data that is kept for a long time and accessed infrequently. It is not for dynamic website assets, active databases, or caching.

questions.question: What does Amazon Elastic Beanstalk provide?

options.text: A PaaS solution to automate application deployment.
A compute engine for Amazon ECS.
A scalable file storage solution for use with AWS and on-premises servers.

questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) that automatically handles deployment, capacity provisioning, load balancing, and scaling for your application. It is not an ECS engine, file store, or NoSQL database.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that performs automated network assessments of Amazon EC2 instances to check for vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector performs automated security assessments of EC2 instances (and other workloads) to detect vulnerabilities and deviations. Security groups and NACLs filter traffic but do not assess vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following controls do customers fully inherit from AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Customers fully inherit environmental controls (D) and physical controls (E) from AWS — AWS owns the data centers entirely. Patch management, database, and training controls are shared or customer responsibilities.

questions.question: A company needs to host a database in Amazon RDS for at least three years. Which of the following options would be the most cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: For a fixed 3-year commitment, a Reserved Instance with Partial Upfront payment delivers a larger discount than No Upfront, making it the most cost-effective of the listed options. On-Demand and Spot are not ideal for a guaranteed multi-year database.

questions.question: Your application has recently experienced significant global growth, and international users are complaining of high latency. What is the AWS characteristic that can help improve your international users’ experience?
questions.explanation: AWS's global reach — deploying in Regions and Edge Locations worldwide — improves the experience for international users by serving them closer to home. Elasticity, durability, and high availability address other concerns.

questions.question: Savings Plans are available for which of the following AWS compute services? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Savings Plans cover Amazon EC2 (D) and AWS Lambda (E) (as well as Fargate). They do not apply to Batch, Outposts, or Lightsail.

questions.question: A company has business critical workloads hosted on AWS and they are unwilling to accept any downtime. Which of the following is a recommended best practice to protect their workloads in the event of an unexpected natural disaster?

options.text: Replicate data across multiple Edge Locations worldwide and use Amazon CloudFront to perform automatic failover in the event of an outage.
Deploy AWS resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same AWS Region.
Create point-in-time backups in another subnet and recover this data when a disaster occurs.
Deploy AWS resources to another AWS Region and implement an Active-Active disaster recovery strategy.

questions.explanation: For zero-downtime protection against a regional disaster, deploy across another AWS Region with an Active-Active strategy so traffic continues if one Region fails. Multiple AZs in one Region do not survive a full-Region disaster, and Edge Locations/subnets are not DR targets.

questions.question: Which statement is correct with regards to AWS service limits? (Choose TWO)

options.text: You can contact AWS support to increase the service limits.
Each IAM user has the same service limit.
There are no service limits on AWS.
You can use the AWS Trusted Advisor to monitor your service limits.
The Amazon Simple Email Service is responsible for sending email notifications when usage approaches a service limit.

questions.explanation: You can contact AWS Support to request a service-limit (quota) increase (A), and AWS Trusted Advisor helps you monitor service limits (D). Limits are not identical per IAM user, and limits do exist.

questions.question: What is the AWS tool that enables you to use scripts to manage all AWS services and resources?
questions.explanation: The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) lets you script and manage all AWS services and resources from the command line. The Console is graphical, and Service Catalog/OpsWorks serve other roles.

questions.question: What are the connectivity options that can be used to build hybrid cloud architectures? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Hybrid connectivity is built with AWS Direct Connect (C), a dedicated private link, and AWS VPN (E), an encrypted tunnel over the internet. Artifact, Cloud9, and CloudTrail are not connectivity options.

questions.question: A company has deployed a new web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Which of the following should they use to ensure that the incoming HTTP traffic is distributed evenly across the instances?
questions.explanation: An Application Load Balancer distributes incoming HTTP/HTTPS (Layer 7) traffic evenly across EC2 instances. Auto Scaling adjusts capacity, NLB operates at Layer 4, and EC2 Auto Recovery restarts single instances.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS offerings is a MySQL-compatible relational database service that can scale capacity automatically based on demand?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database; Aurora Serverless can scale capacity automatically with demand. Neptune is a graph DB, and the RDS engines listed do not auto-scale capacity the same way.

questions.question: Which of the following can help protect your EC2 instances from DDoS attacks? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Security Groups (B) and Network ACLs (E) filter traffic to your EC2 instances and subnets, helping mitigate unwanted/DDoS traffic at the network layer. CloudHSM, Batch, and IAM do not filter network traffic.

questions.question: What is the AWS data warehouse service that supports a high level of query performance on large amounts of datasets?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is AWS's data warehouse, optimized for high-performance analytic queries over large datasets. Kinesis streams data, DynamoDB is NoSQL, and RDS is transactional.

questions.question: Which of the following should be considered when performing a TCO analysis to compare the costs of running an application on AWS instead of on-premises?
questions.explanation: A TCO analysis comparing AWS to on-premises must account for physical hardware costs (servers, storage, networking) that AWS eliminates. Market research and business analysis are not TCO infrastructure factors.

questions.question: How are AWS customers billed for Linux-based Amazon EC2 usage?

options.text: EC2 instances will be billed on one second increments, with a minimum of one minute.
EC2 instances will be billed on one hour increments, with a minimum of one day.
EC2 instances will be billed on one minute increments, with a minimum of one hour.
EC2 instances will be billed on one day increments, with a minimum of one month.

questions.explanation: Linux-based EC2 instances are billed per second, with a one-minute minimum. The other increments do not match AWS's billing.

questions.question: Which of the following will impact the price paid for an EC2 instance? (Choose TWO)

options.text: The Availability Zone where the instance is provisioned.

questions.explanation: EC2 price depends on the instance type (A) and the Region/Availability Zone where it runs (B). Load balancing, number of S3 buckets, and private IP count are not direct EC2 pricing factors.

questions.question: A customer spent a lot of time configuring a newly deployed Amazon EC2 instance. After the workload increases, the customer decides to provision another EC2 instance with an identical configuration. How can the customer achieve this?

options.text: By creating an AWS Config template from the old instance and launching a new instance from it.
By creating an EBS Snapshot of the old instance.
By installing Aurora on EC2 and launching a new instance from it.
By creating an AMI from the old instance and launching a new instance from it.

questions.explanation: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the configured instance and launch new instances from it to reproduce the exact configuration. AWS Config has no 'template' launch, EBS snapshots only capture a volume, and Aurora is a database.

questions.question: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage all of its AWS accounts. Which of the following allows the company to restrict what services and actions are allowed in each individual account?
questions.explanation: AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs), applied via AWS Organizations, restrict which services and actions are permitted in each member account. IAM policies grant within an account, and Fargate is a compute engine.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes the AWS Cloud’s agility?

options.text: AWS allows you to host your applications in multiple regions around the world.
AWS provides customizable hardware at the lowest possible cost.
AWS allows you to provision resources in minutes.
AWS allows you to pay upfront to reduce costs.

questions.explanation: AWS agility means you can provision resources in minutes instead of weeks, accelerating experimentation and delivery. Multi-Region hosting, hardware customization, and upfront payment describe other attributes.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using the Amazon Relational Database Service? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Complete control over the underlying host.
Scales automatically to larger or smaller instance types.
Supports the document and key-value data structure.

questions.explanation: Amazon RDS reduces the administrative burden (A) by managing patching/backups, and provides resizable compute capacity (C). It does not give host-level control, auto-change instance types, or support document/key-value models.

questions.question: What is the connectivity option that uses Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) to establish encrypted connectivity between an on-premises network and the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses IPSec to create an encrypted tunnel between your on-premises network and AWS. Direct Connect is private but not inherently IPSec-encrypted, and an internet gateway provides no encryption.

questions.question: What is the minimum level of AWS support that provides 24x7 access to technical support engineers via phone and chat?
questions.explanation: AWS Business Support is the lowest tier offering 24x7 access to technical support engineers via phone, chat, and email. Developer support is business-hours email only; Basic has no technical engineer access.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to control network traffic in AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Network ACLs (A) control traffic at the subnet level and Security Groups (E) control traffic at the instance level. Key pairs and access keys are credentials, and IAM policies control API permissions, not network traffic.

questions.question: A company has developed a media transcoding application in AWS. The application is designed to recover quickly from hardware failures. Which one of the following types of instance would be the most cost-effective choice to use?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances are the cheapest option and fit a media-transcoding app that recovers quickly from interruptions. Reserved, On-Demand, and Dedicated cost more for this interruptible workload.

questions.question: Which AWS Service provides the current status of all AWS Services in all AWS Regions?
questions.explanation: The AWS Service Health Dashboard shows the current status of all AWS services across all Regions. The Personal Health Dashboard is account-specific, and CloudWatch monitors your own resources.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature can be used to call AWS Services from different programming languages?
questions.explanation: AWS SDKs let you call AWS services programmatically from many languages (Python, Java, JavaScript, etc.). The CLI is command-line, CodeDeploy automates deployments, and the Console is graphical.

questions.question: Which AWS Service can be used to register a new domain name?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 lets you register new domain names (as well as provide DNS and routing). Personalize, KMS, and Config do not register domains.

questions.question: App development companies move their business to AWS to reduce time-to-market and improve customer satisfaction, what are the AWS automation tools that help them deploy their applications faster? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation (A) automates infrastructure provisioning as code, and AWS Elastic Beanstalk (D) automates application deployment; both speed up delivery. Migration Hub, IAM, and Macie are not app-deployment automation tools.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides cost-optimization recommendations?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor provides cost-optimization recommendations (along with checks for performance, security, fault tolerance, and limits). The Pricing Calculator estimates, QuickSight visualizes BI, and X-Ray traces requests.

questions.question: A company has hundreds of VPCs in multiple AWS Regions worldwide. What service does AWS offer to simplify the connection management among the VPCs?
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub to simplify connectivity among hundreds of VPCs (and on-premises) across Regions. VPC Peering is point-to-point and does not scale as simply; security groups and Connect are unrelated.

questions.question: What is one benefit and one drawback of buying a reserved EC2 instance? (Select TWO)

options.text: Instances can be shut down by AWS at any time with no notification.
Reserved instances require at least a one-year pricing commitment.
There is no additional charge for using dedicated instances.
Reserved instances provide a significant discount compared to on-demand instances.
Reserved instances are best suited for periodic workloads.

questions.explanation: A drawback is that Reserved Instances require at least a one-year pricing commitment (B); a benefit is the significant discount versus On-Demand (D). RIs are not shut down arbitrarily and are best for steady, not periodic, workloads.

questions.question: Why does every AWS Region contain multiple Availability Zones?

options.text: Multiple Availability Zones allows you to build resilient and highly available architectures.
Multiple Availability Zones results in lower total cost compared to deploying in a single Availability Zone.
Multiple Availability Zones allows for data replication and global reach.
Multiple Availability Zones within a region increases the storage capacity available in that region.

questions.explanation: Multiple Availability Zones per Region let you build resilient, highly available architectures that survive a single data-center (AZ) failure. They are not primarily about cost, global reach, or raw storage capacity.

questions.question: What is the most cost-effective purchasing option for running a set of EC2 instances that must always be available for a period of two months?
questions.explanation: For instances needed for only two months, On-Demand is most cost-effective because Reserved Instances require a minimum one-year term and Spot cannot guarantee continuous availability.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of running an application in multiple Availability Zones?

options.text: Allows you to exceed AWS service limits.
Reduces application response time between servers and global users.
Increases the availability of your application.

questions.explanation: Running across multiple Availability Zones increases application availability by tolerating the failure of any single AZ. It does not raise service limits, reduce global user latency, or add compute capacity per se.

questions.question: Data security is one of the top priorities of AWS. How does AWS deal with old storage devices that have reached the end of their useful life?

options.text: AWS sells the old devices to other hosting providers.
AWS destroys the old devices in accordance with industry-standard practices.
AWS sends the old devices for remanufacturing.
AWS stores the old devices in a secure place.

questions.explanation: AWS decommissions storage devices at end of life by destroying them following industry-standard practices (e.g., NIST/DoD techniques) so data cannot be recovered. AWS does not sell, remanufacture, or simply store old drives.
